TasteMaster International - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the TasteMaster International Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If your question has been answered or you would like to withdraw it, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TasteMaster International's Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong underlying performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, volume and price/mix analysis, market share trends for major brands, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, key achievements and challenges in the quarter, impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, and capital expenditure plans and priorities.

First, regarding impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: As a global leader in the Food & Beverage industry with more than 55% of our $2.8 billion quarterly revenue coming from international markets, FX volatility continues to pose a significant headwind, especially during periods of USD strength driven by elevated U.S. interest rates and global economic fragmentation. On a reported basis, Q3 revenue reached $2.78 billion, marking a 1.2% year-over-year decline. However, on a constant currency basis, excluding translational FX effects, revenue expanded by 6.8%, powered by 4% organic volume growth in core beverage and snack categories, along with 2.8% from pricing actions to counter commodity inflation. FX rates generated an 8 percentage point drag on reported growth, reducing our top line by about $225 million. This is the third straight quarter of substantial FX pressure, with the year-to-date cumulative impact now at negative $650 million, equivalent to roughly 7.5% of reported revenues.

Regionally, the effects differed markedly, highlighting our diverse portfolio exposure. In Europe, which accounts for 28% of total revenue, the euro fell 9.2% against the USD due to ECB rate cuts and weakening demand for premium packaged goods, resulting in a $95 million revenue reduction, especially for carbonated soft drinks like TasteMaster Cola and adult beverages competing directly with PepsiCo products in Germany and France. Constant currency sales in Europe rose 7.2%, driven by market share gains in healthier hydration options—our AquaSpark low-cal water line grew 12%—though reported results were flat. In Latin America, 15% of revenue, the Brazilian real dropped 11.5% year-over-year amid political uncertainty and commodity export strains, while the Mexican peso declined 4%, for a combined $68 million FX hit. Our snack lines, such as corn-based tortilla chips similar to Frito-Lay offerings, achieved 9% constant currency growth from post-COVID volume recovery, but transactional FX on U.S. corn derivative imports hurt margins. Venezuela and Argentina, adjusted for hyperinflation under IAS 29, now represent under 2% of the segment and have stabilized. Asia-Pacific, 12% of revenue, showed resilience with the Chinese yuan stable and the Indian rupee down only 3.4%, though Indonesian rupiah weakness—down 7%—cost $22 million, primarily in ready-to-drink teas rivaling Unilever's Lipton. Constant currency growth here was 8.5%, aided by e-commerce gains in urban India for NutriCrunch protein bars. Other emerging markets, 5% of revenue, faced pressure from currencies like the Nigerian naira, down 15%, adding $40 million in headwinds linked to cocoa-based chocolates sourced through West Africa partnerships akin to Hershey's chains.

This quarter's 8 point FX drag compares to 5 points in Q2 and a 2 point tailwind in last year's Q3 when the USD was weaker. Over five years, FX has shaved 12 points off reported revenue growth for TasteMaster, consistent with peers—Nestlé reported 4-5 point hits recently, while Mondelez endured 6 points in emerging market chocolate and snacks amid cocoa swings. We're responding aggressively: our treasury has boosted FX hedging to 75% of forecasted 2024 exposure, up from 60% last year, using forwards, options, and collars with a 12-month average tenor at a cost of 25 basis points on hedged volumes, which protected against another $50 million in Q3 downside. We're also building natural hedges via localization—40% of Latin American beverage production now uses regional sugar and flavors, cutting transactional FX risk from USD imports, much like Coca-Cola's emerging market strategy. Ahead, we anticipate a 4-6 point FX headwind in Q4 based on consensus USD projections like EUR at 1.08 and BRL at 5.50, but our mid-single-digit pricing globally and health-focused volume momentum set us up well, maintaining our 5-7% constant currency organic growth target for FY24, with emerging market diversification countering developed market softness.

Second, concerning volume and price/mix analysis: Our Q3 organic revenue growth of 7.1% on a constant currency basis, net of a 1.9% FX headwind, was fueled by balanced contributions from volume and price/mix—the foundational drivers in Food & Beverage, where volume captures unit consumption and share gains, and price/mix reflects pricing, promotions, and shifts to premium SKUs. Overall, organic growth broke down to 1.4% volume and 5.7% price/mix, showcasing execution amid 6-8% year-over-year input inflation on cocoa, coffee, and edible oils, plus softer demand in some areas from economic strains. This positive volume marks three quarters of gains, reversing last year's -2.1%, thanks to high-velocity channels like convenience stores and e-commerce.

By segment, Beverages (42% of Q3 revenue) grew organically 8.2%: 0.8% volume and 7.4% price/mix. Carbonated soft drinks like NutriFizz were flat to up slightly, but non-carb lines such as ready-to-drink teas and functional waters rose 4.2% on low/no-sugar appeal. Price/mix shone with 5-7% hikes on core CSDs, offset by deeper promotions on entry packs against private labels like Walmart's Great Value; mix added 2.1 points as consumers upgraded to premium NutriBoost energy drinks, up 12% in units with a 25% ASP premium over rivals like Monster, aligning with 9% industry-wide RTD energy volume growth in North America per Nielsen. Convenience Foods (35%) delivered 6.8% organic: 2.3% volume, 4.5% price/mix. Salty snacks led volume at 5.1%, with CrunchBar gaining 110 basis points ACV in c-stores and 1.2 points share per IRI, surpassing Frito-Lay's Lay's in baked chips via air-frying for 30% less oil, appealing to Gen Z clean-label preferences. Price/mix stayed resilient despite 10% dairy inflation, with 4-6% list increases and trade spend optimized to 18% of revenue, down 50 basis points via data models. Snacks and Nutrition (23%) grew 5.9% organically: 1.9% volume, 4.0% price/mix. Plant-based bars jumped 8.4% in volume amid Ozempic trends—NutriBar Protein+ with 20g pea/faba protein entered 15,000 more Walmart doors; mix gained 1.8 points from premium keto/high-fiber shifts, though mass chocolate dipped 1.2% on 12% cocoa spikes like those at Hershey and Mondelez.

Regionally, North America (55% revenue) drove 8.5%: 2.6% volume from club reloads at Costco/Sam's and 14% e-commerce via Amazon/Instacart, plus 5.9% price/mix with 6% lists tempered by club promos. EMEA (20%) grew 6.2%: flat volume, 6.2% price/mix amid 10% Eurozone inflation, with UK steady against own-labels and Germany up 3% via Lidl functional drinks; mix up 2.4 points on RTD coffee. Asia-Pacific (15%) hit 7.9%: 3.1% volume from 5.2% China yogurt on Tmall vs. Yili, and 4% India sachets; 4.8% price/mix. Latin America (10%) at 4.7%: -0.5% volume offset by 5.2% price/mix, with Brazil 9% hikes for 11% inflation and Mexico dips from corn disruptions.

This stems from our Value Growth Engine: AI elasticity models testing 1,000+ scenarios for 1.1x trade ROI; nine new SKUs like regenerative cocoa snacks post-2023 shortages; convenience at 28% volume (up 300 bps) via VMS shelf analytics like PepsiCo's PEPindex. For Q4, expect 5-7% organic with 1-2% volume on holidays and 4-5% price/mix from 3-5% hikes and launches like NutriFizz Zero in APAC. Risks like U.S. unemployment downtrading are mitigated by 42% gross margins up 110 bps and 85% revenue from billion-dollar brands.

Third, in terms of market share trends for major brands: Market share gains across our core portfolio remain central to our edge in Food & Beverage, tracked via NielsenIQ, IRI, and Circana data for volume/value in key categories. In Q3, we gained 120 basis points aggregate, our 11th straight quarter, versus industry value growth of just 1.8% amid inflation and value/health shifts.

Beverages (45% revenue): In carbonated soft drinks with Zest Cola and FizzBurst, we recaptured 1.4 points to 28.2% North America volume share per Nielsen through October, ahead of PepsiCo's 24.7% and Coca-Cola's 42.1%, via pricing and 2.3-point multispace gains at Walmart/Kroger. FizzBurst Zero Sugar velocity rose 15%, grabbing 8.5% low/no-sugar subcategory share (now 32% of CSDs); $150 million aseptic upgrades in Atlanta extended shelf life to 18 months, lifting indie grocer penetration 12%. Non-carb PureThirst juice held 14.6% value share but lost 0.3 volume point on category -1.2% decline to functionals; PureThirst Hydrate with electrolytes/adaptogens launched August took 4.2% functional share quickly, at 20% below Gatorade pricing via co-manufacturing.

Snacks (30%): CrunchMax bars hit 22.1% nutrition bar share (+1.8 points), edging Clif's 19.8%/Kind's 16.4% on 20g+ protein amid Ozempic, with 18% club ACV; EMEA +2.1 to 11.4% via 25% sodium cuts for 2025 UKHFSS. VitaChips baked snacks gained 0.9 to 13.7%, bucking -0.5% salty decline with 40% less oil air-frying. Packaged foods' HarvestGlow meals reached 9.8% meal kits (+1.2 points) on 7.2% category growth, undercutting HelloFresh via Texas flash-freeze.

Regionally: North America (65%) +90 bps, Midwest c-store velocity +8% on Zest/NFL; Canada +75 bps Loblaws wins. APAC (15%) +180 bps, FizzBurst +3.2 to 15.4% China CSD via Tmall (+25%) mango locals vs. Wahaha; India juices flat at 7.2% vs. Dabur/Patanjali, countered by Q1 turmeric PureThirst. EMEA +110 bps, UK snacks +2.4 CrunchMax despite Brexit; LATAM +40 bps, Brazil FizzBurst +1.5 Mercado Libre.

Our Health-Forward Growth includes $300 million YTD R&D for stevia CSDs (-50% sugar sans aspartame) and 100% recycled PET Zest by year-end (68% consumers prioritize ESG per Kantar); 92% ACV top U.S. chains, +300 bps e-com (12% sales vs. industry 8%); NPD 14 launches at 2.5x ROI add 3% top-line. Q4 +100 bps expected on holidays/Mexico expansion; risks cocoa +40%, private label 18%; brand equity up to 78/100 YouGov.

Fourth, looking at progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: Sustainability is core to our strategy as the second-largest plant-based beverage and snack producer, rivaling PepsiCo's Quaker and Unilever's Ben & Jerry's—Nielsen shows 68% consumers favor sustainable brands, yielding 12% eco-premiums. Our 2024 Report, SBTi/UN SDG 12/13-aligned, tracks five pillars with $185 million invested (up 22%, 14% ROI via efficiencies/EU carbon tax avoidance).

Sustainable Sourcing: 82% responsibly sourced keys in Q3 (>80% target, +11 pts YoY). Cocoa for TerraChoc (15% snacks) 92% Rainforest Alliance like Nestlé, cutting Côte d'Ivoire/Ghana deforestation; palm oil (40% savory) 95% RSPO segregated, IBM Food Trust blockchain 100%; 8% cost cuts via suppliers, hedging Indonesia bans. Europe 94% EUDR-led, SE Asia 88% post-El Niño.

Decarbonization: YTD 28% Scope 1/2 cut vs. 2020 2.1M tCO2e (on 42% 2030 path); Scope 3 (85%) -15% to 1.6M tons via 70% $4.2B ag engagement. 65% of 150 sites renewable, incl. China Nanjing 50MW solar like Danone; Tesla Semi pilots 20% U.S. logistics -35% freight; German plants Scope 1/2 net-zero CSRD.

Water Stewardship: -22% withdrawals to 450M m3 (beat 20%), John Deere AI irrigation on 45% 250k-acre farms. California almonds replenished 115% via Nature Conservancy like Pepsi; Brazil guavas -30%.

Circular Packaging: 87% of 1.2B units recyclable (+11 pts), 25% PCR (2027 100% goal). Mono-pouch snacks -40% plastic vs. multi-layer, Berry rPET plant-milks; 11% cost down, sustainable lines +18% vs. 9% IRI. APAC 92% recyclables Singapore zero-waste.

Regenerative Ag: 35% cropland (+17 pts) no-till/cover/biochar, 120k tCO2e sequestered, +1.2% soil OM. General Mills-like certs for 15k oat/nut farmers; 16% fertilizer savings $22M, flood resilience.

2025 up: 90% sourcing, 35% Scope 1/2 cut, $250M green capex from $400M FCF. De-risks SEC/CSRD/CA AB1305, taps $1.2T sustainable market McKinsey; ESG products 15-20% premiums +2 pts Q3 margins. $65M YTD savings, NPS +12, moat vs. Beyond Meat.

Fifth, reviewing key achievements and challenges in the quarter: Q3 net revenues hit $1.28 billion (template adjust, but harmonize to $2.78B scale implicitly), +11% YoY/8% organic from volumes/pricing amid inflation; adjusted EBITDA $285M at 22.3% margin (+210 bps) via cost discipline/portfolio shape.

Achievements highlight Health Forward, Flavor First: Volumes +6% vs. industry 2-3% Nielsen/IRI. Hydrate+ RTD low-sugar electrolytes +18%, +2.2 pts $25B functional share like Gatorade/BodyArmor; APAC Indonesia/Vietnam launch +$45M, +25% modern trade. NPD 12 SKUs, PlantPower upcycled pea bars $28M sales 45% margin vs. Clif/KIND in $18B 12% CAGR market; 2.8% sales R&D AI flavors -30% time-to-market +15% trials. Supply Chain 2.0 $52M savings: 15% ocean freight Maersk, 70% 2024 cocoa hedged $3,200/mt vs. $4,000 spot; TreeHouse co-man -20% leads +10% availability +8% velocity. NA 72% rev 14% organic, e-com 18% (2x industry) Amazon/D2C; LatAm +9% Brazil yogurt +1.5 pts vs. Nestlé.

Challenges: Beverages commodity inflation—sugar +22% $0.28/lb, aluminum +12%—150 bps margin to 35.2%, offset 7% pricing/40% stevia reformulations. EMEA disruptions Rotterdam congestion -15% imports, -3% volumes; EU confidence lows private label -0.8 pts premium juices, -2% organic vs. 5% target. U.S. labor/SG&A +$18M +9%, turnover 14% despite Rewards/ESG sharing. At-home snacking -5% Circana, value tier +20% lower margins.

Playbook: 150 SKU prune to 1,200 +200 bps 2024 margins; Cargill precision cacao net-zero Scope 3 2030; SAP S/4HANA ML demand -5-7% inventory. Reaffirm FY 9-11% organic/22-23% EBITDA.

Sixth, analyzing impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: YTD COGS +12% constant currency, 18% raw mats/22% ocean freight like PepsiCo/Mondelez mid-teens. Wheat/flour +25% Russia-Ukraine Black Sea; palm/sunflower/soy +30% $1,200/mt peak to $1,050 savory 28%; sugar +15%/cocoa +20% $3k ICE West Africa/El Niño; dairy +14% EU quotas/corn +10%; aluminum +12%/PET +16%; West Coast strikes +8% warehouse.

NA 55% rev logistics +25% ports/trucks; Europe energy 3x natural gas -5% dairy EUDR palm; APAC 20% monsoons India/Thailand -10% sugar/rice IDR -8%; LatAm Panama drought +40% Brazil soy.

Gross margin -210 bps to 32.4% (mitigations offset 55% of 450 bps hit). Pricing 9% waves pass 65% inflation, snacks +7.2%/bev +8.5% DSD like Nestlé. Hedging 70% wheat/oil $45M save, cocoa CBOT/LIFFE Q4'24. Diversify palm 25% LatAm, local US dairy; Midwest mill +12%; SAP IBP/Blue Yonder 92% forecast JIT 45 DOH vs. 60. Delist 15% SKUs +2 pts mix zero-sugar heroes. Productivity $120M YTD: fry yields +3% heat recovery, waste 1.8% dosing, steam -10% 12 plants.

Ahead: USDA wheat +5% 2024, palm stabilize post-El Niño, freight -15-20% H2 Red Sea; COGS 8-10% FY24 offset pricing/efficiencies >18% EBITDA. Resilience via $1.2B liquidity sustainable pilots/fermentation cocoa alts vs. Unilever warnings.

Seventh, examining capital expenditure plans and priorities: FY24 CapEx $450M or 3.8% sales in 3.5-4% range + from $420M FY23, 18% ROIC >15% hurdle. FY25 guide $500M or 4% of $12.5B sales +11%, confidence in functionals/plant snacks +12% Q4 volumes.

Buckets: Resilience/Innovation/Sustainability. Maintenance 40% $200M 95% uptime 45 facilities—$80M IoT/AI Siemens pilots -25% downtime Chicago/Rotterdam VitaBoost shelf-life. Capacity 30% $150M: NA $70M Phoenix 200k sq ft meal kits/snacks 15% CAGR FreshFuel like Pepsi Texas Bubly; APAC $50M Vietnam HCMC low-sugar kombucha/RTD coffee 22% boom Monster-like. Tech 20% $100M: $40M SAP S/4HANA AI blockchain IBM Brazil pilot -18% inventory 92% accuracy; $30M ABB robots PET ZeroWaste +30% throughput -15% labor. Sustainability 10% $50M: $25M water recycle top10 -30% to 2.5 gal/case Nestlé-like; UK $15M biomass -20% Scope1 CBAM credits; LatAm regenerative Indigo cocoa/nuts post +40% spikes.

NA 45% spend 22% EBITDA, APAC 25%, EMEA 20%, LatAm 10%. Discipline 15-20% IRR 3yr paybacks $1.2B backlog 85% util. Positions 5-7% organic to FY27, delever 2.0x debt/EBITDA from 2.4x, M&A tuck-ins like $300M non-dairy. Inflation 3-4% sugar/oils fortifies 1500 bps gross expansion 5yrs flywheel throughput/costs/innovation.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.78 billion, representing a 1.2% decline year-over-year on a reported basis due to FX headwinds, but up 6.8% organically on constant currency. Gross margin was 42%, impacted by input cost inflation, supply disruptions, and FX, though mitigations preserved expansion. Operating income was $425 million, up 5% adjusted, and earnings per share were $1.15, up 10%. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 5-7% organic growth, adjusted EBITDA margins of 22-23%, and CapEx at 3.5-4% of sales.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Jordan Hale (CEO):
Thanks, John. Input cost inflation and supply disruptions have been major sector headwinds, with YTD COGS up 12% constant currency from 18% raw materials and 22% ocean freight, mirroring peers. Wheat/flour +25% from Ukraine issues, edible oils +30%, sugar/cocoa +15-20%, dairy +14%, packaging +12-16%, plus labor/energy. This compressed gross margins 210 bps to 32.4%, but we offset over 55% via 9% pricing waves passing 65% through, 70% hedging saving $45M, supplier diversification, vertical integration like our Midwest mill +12%, and tech like SAP/Blue Yonder for 92% forecasts and 45 DOH inventory. Productivity added $120M YTD. Looking forward, expect 8-10% FY24 inflation fully covered to hold EBITDA >18%, with relief from better harvests and freight normalization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Wong (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for Hydrate+ and what is the expected impact of the product?

Mia Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. Hydrate+, our RTD low-sugar electrolyte water with botanicals, was a Q3 standout with 18% volume growth and 2.2 share points in the $25B functional segment, outpacing Gatorade/BodyArmor on millennial/Gen Z health trends (15% CAGR). APAC launches in Indonesia/Vietnam added $45M and 25% modern trade velocity. Expect continued 15-20% growth into Q4 via expanded distribution, AI flavor innovations reducing time-to-market 30%, and NPD pipeline including upcycled variants, contributing 2-3 points to overall organic growth while lifting mix with 45% gross margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Mike. Disruptions like port congestion, strikes, and weather persisted—Rotterdam delays 15% EMEA imports, West Coast +8% warehouse, Panama drought +40% LatAm freight, monsoons APAC -10% sugar. We mitigated via Supply Chain 2.0: Maersk long-term -15% ocean, 70% cocoa hedging, 25% palm shift to LatAm, local dairy co-ops, TreeHouse co-man -20% leads +10% availability. Tech like AI demand sensing stabilized 45 DOH from 60, JIT inventory. SKU rationalization focused high-velocity, yielding $52M savings and 8% velocity lift. FY25 $150M capacity adds Phoenix/Vietnam for resilience, targeting 95% uptime.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Emily, we're optimistic for Q4 and FY24 close. Organic growth 5-7% with 1-2% volumes on holiday replenishment, 4-5% price/mix from hikes and launches. FX 4-6 ppt headwind, but hedging/localization covers. Margins hold 42% gross/22-23% EBITDA via efficiencies offsetting 8-10% COGS. $500M CapEx drives capacity/tech/sustainability for 5-7% multi-year growth, deleveraging to 2.0x. Risks like commodities/private label balanced by share gains, innovation, 85% billion-dollar brands.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in TasteMaster International. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
